prompt.alinti: Ever wonder how software companies actually find their security holes?
Most businesses only pay for a professional hacker to test their security once a year, so they're basically leaving the front door unlocked for the other 364 days.
That's where this tool, called Shannon, steps in to change the game.
It's an automated AI that acts just like a security guard for your computer code, constantly checking for weaknesses before your work even hits the public.
Think of it like a smart home security system that doesn't just watch the door, but actively tries to pick the locks to see if they're actually secure.
It looks through the internal structure of your website or app, finds any potential entry points, and runs actual tests to prove if someone could break in.
You get to sleep better knowing that the software you're building has been poked and prodded by an AI that doesn't take breaks.
It's a clever way to stay one step ahead of anyone looking to cause trouble.
Check out the project on the KeyGraph HQ Shannon GitHub page.
Shannon is an autonomous, AI pentester for web applications and APIs.
It analyzes your source code, identifies attack vectors, and executes real exploits to prove vulnerabilities before they reach production.
This repository is Shannon Open Source: the full agent, run locally from your command line.
AI agents and LLMs: start with llms.txt for a concise map of this repository, or use llms-full.txt for the README and docs combined into one file.
